jurisdictions.name: Reno
jurisdictions.office: City of Reno Development Services (Building and Safety)
jurisdictions.portal_name: ONE Regional Licensing and Permits (Accela Citizen Access)
notes: Reno publishes a Residential Pool Submittal Guidelines sheet; plans must show barriers, fences and gates, including height, openings and latches.
The same sheet asks for pool equipment spec sheets, pipe and conduit installation depth, an equipotential bonding detail, and gas piping sizing calculations.
It also asks for electrical load calculations, circuits and GFCI protection, structural calculations for a cast-in-place pool, and manufacturer installation instructions for a fiberglass pool.
All building permit applications go in electronically through the ONE portal; since January 1, 2026 plans are accepted only under the 2024 edition of the building codes.

jurisdictions.name: Las Vegas
jurisdictions.office: City of Las Vegas Building and Safety
notes: Permits that need plans are applied for through the Dashboard (Citizen Portal); permits without plans use the Online Building Permits page.
The city requires all new commercial, residential and civil building plans to be submitted electronically.
The city says it adopted the 2021 International Building Code and International Fire Code, effective March 23, 2023.
The building permits page does not mention pools, so pool-specific questions go to Customer Service.

jurisdictions.name: Clark County (unincorporated Las Vegas Valley)
notes: Building & Fire Prevention takes permit applications through the Citizen Access Portal.
The plan submittal section lists 'Do I Need a Permit?', how-to guides, application forms and a plan submittal FAQ.
An owner who intends to construct, enlarge, alter or repair a structure must first apply for a permit; exemptions are in Building Administrative Code section 22.02.190.

jurisdictions.name: Henderson (Clark County)
jurisdictions.office: City of Henderson Department of Building and Fire Safety
jurisdictions.portal_name: Apply for Building, Fire and Civil Permits (DSC Online)
notes: The city's Swimming Pool Site Details sheet is B-110, a Southern Nevada Building Officials regional standard for the 2024 ISPSC. It says a gate less than 8 feet wide must be self-closing and self-latching and open outward. Its gate note says the gate must be at least 60 inches high above adjacent grade, with no more than 4 inches between grade and the bottom of the gate.
The same sheet says that, per ISPSC Section 327.2, a pool closer than 5.0 feet to a building or structure may be permitted when substantiated by a Nevada licensed civil or structural engineer.

The city's residential pool and spa inspection handout says custom (concrete and site-built) and prefabricated (ceramic/fiberglass) pools and spas typically need three groups of inspections. At the final pool inspection, the inspector checks items including labeling, clearances, secured bonding, required drainage, permanent barriers, a self-latching gate, lighting and a handhold or bench.

The city's Swimming Pools and Spas standard designs page lists, under its 2024 codes (effective on submittals received on or after January 2, 2026), B-110 for pool setbacks and details, B-109 for when safety glazing is required near a pool, and BFS-5 for the pool safety barrier.

jurisdictions.name: North Las Vegas (Clark County)
jurisdictions.office: City of North Las Vegas Building Safety Division
notes: The city's Application for Pool Permit asks for the square feet, gallons and average depth of the pool and the spa, and the square feet of decking. It also asks for the existing electrical service size, the feet of underground electrical and the conduit diameter, and the gas line type, heater BTUs and the length and diameter of the gas pipe. If access to the construction area involves an adjacent property, the adjacent property owner must complete a Property Line Authorization Form.

The city posts the Southern Nevada Amendments to the 2024 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code (ISPSC). For one- and two-family dwellings, the top of the barrier must be at least 60 inches above grade, measured on the side of the barrier that faces away from the pool or spa. At a residential pool or spa, a door or gate latch release that is reached from outside the barrier and is not self-locking must be at least 54 inches above the finished floor or ground.

Under Section 327.2 of those amendments, a pool or spa may not be placed closer than 60 inches to a building or structure and may not encroach within public utility easements. An exception may be permitted when a Nevada licensed structural or civil engineer provides substantiation that no damage will occur to buildings, structures or adjacent properties and that no unsafe structural conditions will exist.

The city's Current Adopted Codes and Ordinances page lists the 2024 ISPSC, 2024 International Residential Code, 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code and 2023 National Electrical Code. Each is listed with Southern Nevada amendments.
